why: Slice 2 of docs/plan/quests/law-options-0580-PLAN.md, next/ only (libfabrika's tests). The shared property runner's 22 calls in 13 files (the count the plan gives, re-counted on the branch at 492feb546 with rg for a property( call not after a dot, Testing.test-support.ts and settings/StartsTest.ts left out) moved from property in Testing.test-support.ts to the package's it.effect.prop or it.live.prop, imported from @kampus/vitest. Each call became the .prop of the member it sat in (it.effect or it.live), so the eight it.live laws in node/client stay on the live services. The 22 calls are 23 laws: the hands start's law factory was one call that made both H2 and H5, and both are now written out with their titles, so the plant check can read them. Every fast-check input is kept unchanged as the property's one input, with the plan's ordering reason line, and seed 119120 comes from the package. Each law's plant is its plant option; three title labels moved to options (Mail.test.ts format, LedgerTurnReads.test.ts pinned 936, CommandsNode.laws.test.ts vector), and the plant sentences in file comments went. No law was loosened. The old laws checked their coverage once after the property ended (an empty walk cannot pass); the package's .prop has no step after the last case, so each such file keeps that same check with vitest's onTestFinished, registered by the first case and run once when the law ends (a helper named reach, written in each file because the plan gives the tests step no shared file). Two things are left for the build: layer-rules.json's next-permissions row must import next-vitest (lint:layers fails on RelationsTest.ts:13, the only lint failure), and plant.ts records a shared suite's law under the test file that runs the suite, not the *Test.ts file that declares it, so the plant check cannot match the 9 suite laws' records.

plants.law: L3: in any log over three streams with reused ids, get equals read's first entry under the id, and head equals read's last rev or 0
plants.plant: head(stream) answers the largest rev over every stream: its query reads WHERE stream = ? OR 1

plants.law: T1041 L7 ledger: over appends to several streams, end is the pos of the last entry read returns, none for an empty stream, and returns the same bytes whatever the newest entry's body size
plants.plant: end(stream) answers the newest pos over every stream: its query reads WHERE stream = ? OR 1

plants.law: L8: the memory and ledger layers agree on every tuple, with resent ids and another writer's rows
plants.plant: the memory layer ignores unrelated rows when it folds (RelationsMemory.ts)

plants.law: L5: after a load every save returns one row from SQL, however many receipts are kept; a save with no load before it returns 1 + n rows once, then 1
plants.plant: a save never answers from the receipt rows it knows: it reads every receipt row each time

plants.law: L6: one long-lived store leaves the same rows and answers as a fresh store per call, across failed saves and a second store's writes
plants.plant: the long-lived store answers from the receipt rows it knows even after another store moved the generation

plants.law: L7: a save that changes no row writes no row, through the same store, after a load, or a fresh one
plants.plant: every save writes its generation row, a save that changes nothing included

plants.law: L1: a new delivery returns as many rows after h earlier letters to the same target as after none
plants.plant: a delivery finds its saved receipt by reading the whole outbox, not by its id

plants.law: L2: a repeat delivery of an accepted command returns the same rows whatever the history, and answers the first receipt
plants.plant: a repeat delivery finds its first letter by reading the whole inbox, not by its id

plants.law: T1041 L7: a new delivery returns as many rows whatever the inbox and the acked stream hold, the cap's reads included
plants.plant: the cap learns where the inbox ends by reading the whole inbox, not by its end

plants.law: T1041 L7: a new delivery returns the same bytes whatever the size of the inbox's newest letter, up to a 1 MiB chunk
plants.plant: the cap learns where the inbox ends by reading its newest letter whole

plants.law: O1: the hello carries the os the start was given, for every value the wire accepts
plants.plant: the hello sends os: "unknown" whatever the start was given

plants.law: H2: after a cut at any journal or call boundary and a restart, the task ends finished with the fake's result when the journal held one, and with unknown interrupted when it held executing and no result
plants.plant: journal_write answers saved and writes nothing, so a restart finds no entry

plants.law: H5: a dropped link during executing or saving lets the local work finish; on reconnect the client lists, takes and reports it, and runs nothing again
plants.plant: execute runs its command twice

plants.law: L4: mail.unread and mail.chunk read through their declarations in the common source order, a byte size is written as text, a value out of range fails naming its key, and an empty file gives the default
plants.plant: mail.unread's schema takes 16385, one past the cap's bound

plants.law: K1: on an empty folder the first current(null) answers created, every later one reused with the same fingerprint; current(stored) answers replaced with a new one; a damaged file is a read error and is left as it was; a file with group or other bits is a read error and is never used
plants.plant: a key file with group or other bits is used, not refused

plants.law: K2: the key file's identity passes the door's own hello check: its raw, fingerprint and line agree, and a hello signed with its sign is admitted
plants.plant: the fingerprint is computed over the key line instead of the raw public bytes

plants.law: K3: on the real file system the key file and its folder are made with modes 0600 and 0700, and two layers opening one empty folder at once end with one key
plants.plant: the key file is written with mode 0644, not 0600

plants.law: J1: the 4a journal over JournalSqlite on :memory: reads exactly what the same writes give over KeyValueStore.layerMemory, and a value that is no entry is bad_entry on both
plants.plant: the journal table has no PRIMARY KEY, so an overwrite adds a second row

plants.law: J2: a hands-like child that saves all sixteen keys, then writes in a loop and is killed with SIGKILL at a generated moment, leaves every one of the sixteen keys holding one whole entry when the file is opened again
plants.plant: set deletes the key, waits a millisecond, then inserts, so a kill between the two loses the entry

plants.law: S2 property: [secrets] over generated flows (keys created, reused and replaced, knocks and hellos refused, a key removed with 4003, key files that fail to read, commands that fail), the private half in base64url, base64 or hex is in no frame the client wrote, no span, no log line, no error, no journal row and no state the run held
plants.plant: the key file's loaded identity answers the private half as raw, so the hello sends it

plants.law: C1: execute answers exited { code, version } for a child that exits, failed spawn_failed when the spawn fails, failed output_limit with the child's scope closed once stdout and stderr together pass the cap, and never an error or a defect
plants.plant: only stdout counts toward the output cap

plants.law: C2: [secrets] the spawned command is git with argv [--version], extendEnv false and env holding only PATH; a planted secret in the hands' environment never reaches the child
plants.plant: the child is spawned with extendEnv: true

plants.law: C3: has is [git] exactly when a PATH folder holds a file named git with an execute bit, and [] otherwise
plants.plant: has reports git for a file on PATH without an execute bit
